title: A DNA Amplicon Sequence Data Processing and Analysis Pipeline for Environmental Microbiomes
author: Kathryn F. Atherton

steps.title: Trim primers and filter reads
steps.instruction: Run cutadapt on each raw sequence to remove primer sequences and discard any read shorter than 50 base pairs.

steps.title: Denoise and infer ASVs
steps.instruction: Execute DADA2 within the BU16S‑ITS pipeline to infer amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) that are 99 % similar in rDNA sequence.

steps.title: Classify ASVs against reference databases
steps.instruction: Use VSEARCH to assign each ASV to SILVA99 (bacterial, version 138.1) or UNITE dynamic database (fungal, version 9.0); keep assignments with ≥95 % sequence identity and give each ASV a unique hash identifier.

steps.title: Combine tables and create phyloseq objects
steps.instruction: Merge all ASV count tables and taxonomy tables from every sequencing run into a single dataset, then split this dataset by sample type (e.g., soil, leaf) and convert each subset into a phyloseq object for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Assign functional groups and pathogen status
steps.instruction: Match fungal genera to the FungalTraits database to assign Primary Lifestyle; compare bacterial taxonomy to an in‑house functional database containing pathways (copiotroph, oligotroph, cellulolytic, ligninolytic, methanotroph, chitinolytic, assimilatory/dissimilatory nitrite‑reducing, assimilatory/dissimilatory nitrate‑reducing); identify fungal plant pathogens (plant‑pathogenic capacity) and animal pathogens (animal‑biotrophic capacity) via FungalTraits; map bacterial representative sequences to the Multiple Bacterial Pathogen Detection database with blastn and label as pathogens when identity ≥95 %.

steps.title: Remove contaminant ASVs
steps.instruction: Apply the decontam R package: use the “prevalence” method to flag ASVs more common in negative controls than in samples; for samples lacking a sequenced negative control, use the “frequency” method comparing ASV frequency to the sample’s DNA concentration; remove all flagged ASVs and also discard any ASVs annotated to non‑bacterial/archaeal taxa (16S) or non‑fungal taxa (ITS).

steps.title: Identify and discard low‑read outliers
steps.instruction: In phyloseq format, calculate an Aitchison distance matrix from the raw ASV table, visualize it with NMDS labeling points by sample ID, and iteratively remove low‑read samples that appear as outliers; repeat NMDS until no low‑read outliers remain, yielding a curated dataset.

steps.title: Determine optimal read‑depth thresholds
steps.instruction: For the curated dataset, generate a second NMDS plot colored by sample properties (e.g., habitat, spatial distance); if beta‑diversity patterns are unsatisfactory, return to the outlier‑removal step using alternative read‑depth thresholds; choose the threshold that removes low‑read samples while preserving sample representation across environmental conditions.

steps.title: Assess and correct batch effects
steps.instruction: Compute an Aitchison distance matrix of the untransformed data and run PERMANOVA with adonis2 (vegan) to test variables such as sequencing run and sample type; plot NMDS colored by the tested variables; optionally perform batch correction with ComBat_seq (sva), defining batch = sample type and preserving environmental covariates (e.g., tree age, site type); keep the corrected ASV table for downstream steps.

steps.title: Generate CLR, Z‑score, and rarefied tables
steps.instruction: From the curated (and optionally batch‑corrected) ASV table, create three transformed datasets: (a) CLR transformation producing a CLR‑transformed table and its Aitchison dissimilarity matrix; (b) Z‑score transformation; (c) rarefaction using phyloseq::rarefy_even_depth, selecting a read count per sample type that minimizes dropped samples while maximizing reads per sample.

steps.title: Add pseudocount and compute Aitchison distances
steps.instruction: Add a pseudocount of 1 to every value in each transformed table before calculating Aitchison distance matrices for beta‑diversity analyses.

steps.title: Calculate Shannon alpha diversity
steps.instruction: Using the rarefied dataset, compute Shannon alpha diversity for each amplicon community with the vegan package in R.

steps.title: Compute functional guild relative abundances
steps.instruction: Convert rarefied ASV counts to percent relative abundances by dividing each ASV count by the total reads in its sample; sum the percentages for all ASVs assigned to each functional guild to obtain guild‑level relative abundances.
